# agentHost: apply managed model defaults without locking choices

Expose the runtime's `model`, `autoTier`, `effortLevel`, and `contextTier` startup defaults in the Copilot Agent Host picker. Managed defaults take precedence over inherited personal preferences in new chats, while explicit current-chat choices and existing conversations retain their configuration.

Use `enableManagedSettings` without the separate `enforceManagedModelDefaults` opt-in. A server-normalized scalar is not evidence of a user lock. Permission/sandbox enforcement and genuinely read-only options advertised by other hosts are unchanged. Ensemble managed-settings integration is out of scope.

## Scenarios and Precedence

| Scenario | Expected Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| New chat, supported managed default, conflicting saved preference | Managed startup default wins. Auto / Intelligence wins over saved Efficiency; no fresh profile is required. |
| User changes model, tier, effort, or context in this chat | Explicit current-chat choice wins, including edits after draft initialization and before the first send. Notification actions use the same scoped configuration as the picker. |
| Return to a chat with an available attached model | Preserve its model and applied configuration, including previously implicit defaults. Validate restored choices against that chat's schema. |
| Existing chat's model is conclusively unavailable | Use an available managed model default; do not copy the old model's effort/context options to its replacement. A pending catalog is not proof of unavailability. |
| Automation template explicitly references an unavailable model | Preserve the template and unavailable selection until the user chooses another model. |
| No applicable managed default | Use saved personal preferences, then built-in defaults. Existing `chat.defaultModel` behavior remains the model-selection fallback. A scoped report without managed defaults does not inherit root managed keys. |
| Managed model or option is unavailable / unsupported | Do not invent a picker choice or project options onto an unrelated model. Runtime resolution remains authoritative; see the unsupported-effort caveat below. |
| Managed default is removed | New chats can use saved personal preferences again. Untouched managed defaults are not persisted as personal choices; existing chats keep their own configuration. |
| Reset with both read-only and editable options | Reset only editable properties; retain host-owned values and write protection. |

Reports are exact-chat-scoped, coalesced, and asynchronous: readback does not block a completed model change. Catalog refreshes update live reports rather than retaining launch-time choices.

## Manual Validation

The maintainer reports that manual testing works in the freshly built Code OSS preview at head `bd6fe32086d1f5b44298c7e32fa9d2a63dc44e42`. Individual cases were not enumerated, so this is a successful user-reported smoke test, not a claim that every scenario below was independently verified.

Use plain, server-shaped payloads with the native test rig. Restart Agent Host after changing policy. Test both a fresh profile and an existing profile with a conflicting saved preference.

```json
{ "model": "auto", "autoTier": "intelligence" }
```

Start a new chat with saved Efficiency: expect editable Auto / Intelligence. Choose Balance or Efficiency, send a short prompt, and verify the choice does not snap back. Another model remains selectable.

```json
{ "model": "gpt-5", "effortLevel": "high", "contextTier": "long_context" }
```

Replace `gpt-5` with an available model offering both options. Expect editable High effort and long context. After draft initialization, change both and send: the edited values must remain selected. Switch between two chats and reload: each retains its configuration. Remove policy with `{}` and restart: new chats use personal preferences rather than retaining an untouched managed default.

The SDK suite rejects conflicting native model/permission policy before testing synthetic server settings. An isolated home alone does not isolate machine-wide device policy; unrelated device controls do not block these scenarios.

## Runtime Caveats

- [github/copilot-agent-runtime#26681](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/26681): unsupported effort still reaches inference in the bundled runtime's default-only mode. Its characterization test reproduces the limitation; it is not a fix. Use supported model/effort combinations.
- [github/copilot-agent-runtime#26739](https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/issues/26739): conflicting-lock resume belongs to the separate strict SDK mode, not enabled here. Default-only resume has independent coverage.
- Upstream picker normalization can move HydraFusion to Ensemble High when `intelligenceUsesHydraFusion` is false. This predates this PR and is separate from managed-default precedence. A general GPT/Claude-to-Ensemble reset has not been reproduced.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed await is directly on _changeModelOnce's sequenced path, and AgentSideEffects awaits changeModel in Promise.all before progressing the turn. The only uncertainty is the typical duration of native/server policy resolution, not reachability or blocking behavior.
Findings.PerformanceResource: SDK IPC plus possible native MDM/GitHub policy I/O
Findings.PerformanceScaling: One new awaited resolution per turn carrying a model selection (and per explicit model change), with retries able to repeat it; cost grows with prompt frequency rather than only policy changes.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased prompt-send and model-switch latency on the critical path
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The same path resolved the chat entry and immediately called entry.setModel using the supplied configuration; it performed no managed-settings query before the turn could proceed.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each live-chat model application now performs and awaits a managed-settings RPC before invoking session.setModel.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added await at RIGHT line 7073 resolves managed settings before the existing entry.setModel call; the pre-diff code proceeded directly from resolving the chat entry to setModel.
Findings.Title: Remove policy resolution from every prompt's critical path
Findings.Impact: A normal prompt carrying the selected model, or an explicit picker change, can be delayed by an additional policy resolution before session.setModel and before the turn is sent; a slow policy source can add up to 3.5 seconds per request.
Findings.Evidence: resolveCopilotManagedSettings crosses the SDK RPC boundary and may wait for native MDM or GitHub policy resolution, with COPILOT_MANAGED_SETTINGS_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS set to 3500 ms. AgentHostSessionHandler attaches the selected model to outgoing turns, and AgentSideEffects calls and awaits agent.chats.changeModel whenever message.model is present before the provider send. The session launch already resolves the same token/working-directory policy, but that result is not retained for subsequent sends.
Findings.Recommendation: Retain the launch/latest session-scoped policy keyed by token and working directory, update it on managed-settings notifications, and use that snapshot for model-option omission; coalesce any required refresh off the send critical path.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The source order proves serialization, _listModels is documented and implemented as a real models.list request, and _publishModels cannot run until the new await completes. Policy latency magnitude varies, but the added critical-path dependency is certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: sequential SDK IPC/network operations for models.list and managed-settings resolution
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Adds one full policy-resolution latency to every catalog refresh; on slow native or GitHub policy sources the added delay is bounded only by the 3.5-second timeout.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: A successful _listModels result was published immediately; catalog readiness paid only the models.list latency.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: A catalog refresh now serially waits for managed-settings resolution after the model-list RPC before publishing any models.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 3070 adds a second awaited boundary only after _listModels has completed, while model publication remains below both awaits.
Findings.Title: Resolve catalog policy in parallel with model discovery
Findings.Impact: On cold startup, sign-in, SDK reload, or catalog refresh, the model picker and dependent session setup remain unavailable for an extra policy-query duration after model discovery already finished.
Findings.Evidence: _refreshModels first awaits client.rpc.models.list via _listModels, then awaits resolveCopilotManagedSettings with a 3.5-second timeout, and only afterward updates _models. refreshModels is used during SDK setup/reload and authentication-driven catalog loading, so picker availability waits for the sum of two independent boundary latencies. Neither result depends on the other.
Findings.Recommendation: Start models.list and managed-settings resolution together and await them with Promise.all before the single atomic publication, preserving the requirement that projected defaults accompany the first published catalog.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The loop, live-chat cardinality, and three-RPC callee are explicit. Each chat has only a per-chat Throttler, so simultaneous calls across distinct chats are not globally limited. The exact number of concurrently live chats varies by workload, affecting severity but not mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: three SDK RPCs plus a session-config dispatch per live chat
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For L live chats, one publication adds 3L sequential-per-chat RPCs launched concurrently across chats, plus L report updates; no aggregate limiter bounds the burst.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: burst IPC/network load and reduced control-plane throughput
Findings.PreviousBehavior: _publishModels only recomputed and published the shared model array; its cost did not scale through SDK control-plane calls with the number of live chats.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every catalog/BYOK/local-row publication now starts a report refresh for all live chats. Each refresh performs managedSettings.resolve, session.model.list, and session.model.getCurrent sequentially, then dispatches a session-config report.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The new loop at RIGHT line 3134 invokes refreshModelConfiguration for every live chat each time _publishModels runs; no such per-chat work existed before.
Findings.Title: Avoid per-chat RPC bursts on every model publication
Findings.Impact: Users with multiple live chats can see bursts of SDK subprocess/policy traffic and report serialization during catalog or local/BYOK model updates, contending with active turns and reducing responsiveness.
Findings.Evidence: _publishModels is called by periodic catalog refreshes (30-minute scheduler for active providers), BYOK bridge changes, local model-row changes, and client restart paths. The added loop covers all _chatEntriesBySdkId. CopilotAgentSession._refreshManagedModelConfiguration then crosses three SDK control-plane boundaries in sequence. Per-session Throttler coalesces only repeated work for the same chat and provides no shared limiter or policy-query grouping across chats.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the latest policy/current-model snapshot per chat and recompute reports locally on catalog changes; only perform boundary reads on actual session model or managed-policy changes. If reads remain necessary, coalesce policy resolution by token/working directory and apply a shared concurrency limit.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cold startup, sign-in/reload, and periodic model-catalog refresh
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Initial authentication/SDK setup cannot publish the model catalog until models.list and then the newly added managed-settings query both complete. Per-chat report refreshes happen after publication and are off the initial catalog critical path, but contend with warm live sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One models.list RPC per coalesced catalog refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the sole remote catalog boundary before publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks catalog publication and picker readiness.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve native/GitHub managed settings through the SDK subprocess.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No policy-resolution boundary existed between successful model discovery and publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Newly blocks publication after models.list has already completed, for up to the 3.5-second timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: managedSettings.resolve, session.model.list, session.model.getCurrent, then session-config dispatch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three RPCs and one config report per live chat, so 3L RPCs for L live chats after one publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Publishing the shared model array did not invoke per-chat control-plane operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off cold startup when L=0; on warm refresh it creates concurrent control-plane load that can contend with active chats.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cold or periodic refresh; warm cost additionally scales with L live chat sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: models.list and managedSettings.resolve are serialized. After publication, all live chats start refreshes concurrently; each chat serializes its own three RPCs with a Throttler, but there is no cross-chat limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing catalog refresh promise coalesces concurrent refresh callers and preserves the last good catalog, but the new managed-policy lookup has no host-side cache and runs on every refresh. Cold startup has no report cache; warm publication re-reads every live chat's policy/current model even when only the shared catalog changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: source ordering, scheduler cadence, call graph, per-chat throttling scope, and RPC cardinality are directly established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native/server policy latency and the number of simultaneously live chats vary; the sequential dependency and 3L warm fan-out are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: the diff serializes an independent policy boundary on catalog readiness and introduces an unbounded per-live-chat RPC burst after publication.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending a prompt or changing model in a live Agent Host chat
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentSideEffects waits for changeModel before provider send. The new managed-settings await occurs before the existing session.setModel RPC, so prompt progress is blocked by both in sequence. Report readback after setModel is asynchronous and off this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve managed settings for the chat working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One new resolution for every turn whose message carries the selected model, plus explicit model changes; retries can repeat it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The chat entry proceeded directly to session.setModel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks session.setModel and the subsequent provider send, up to the 3.5-second policy timeout.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Apply model/effort/context/tier to the runtime session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One setModel per request carrying model selection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the only runtime model-change boundary on the path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Already blocked the model-selection stage before send; the diff places policy resolution in front of it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read policy, model schema, and current model for report publication.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At least one coalesced pipeline after a model-change burst: policy resolve, model.list, and getCurrent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No report-readback boundaries ran after setModel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous report work does not block completed setModel, but consumes SDK control-plane capacity.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of prompts carrying model selections and explicit picker changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Operations for one chat are serialized by the chat queue. One policy query and one setModel run sequentially per request; distinct chats may resolve policy concurrently without a shared limiter.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The session launch already resolves policy for the same token and working directory, and report refreshes obtain later snapshots, but neither is retained for changeModel. Consequently every request carrying a model selection performs a fresh resolution; there is no positive-result cache or in-flight coalescing by token/directory.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: outgoing selected models are attached in AgentHostSessionHandler, AgentSideEffects awaits changeModel before send, and the added query precedes setModel.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The workbench normally supplies a selected model, but some host-default requests may omit it; policy sources may resolve quickly in common deployments. The blocking await and timeout are not uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable: a repeated policy RPC is newly added to the per-turn critical path despite an existing session-scoped resolution.

Scenarios.Scenario: Live managed-policy/model changes and chat-scoped picker report updates
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Managed-settings and session-model events schedule asynchronous readback. Picker state updates after the report dispatch; the report does not block session.setModel, but SDK control-plane work and AHP updates share resources with active turns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve policy, list session models, read current model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One three-RPC refresh per chat per settled trigger burst; catalog publication can trigger all live chats together.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No chat-scoped runtime model report or associated RPCs existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the completed model-change critical path but on the path to live report/picker readback.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One server action when a report differs; the patch includes the complete chat-keyed reports object for that owner session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No model-report payload was serialized into session config.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Propagates report state to connected clients and adds serialization/protocol traffic.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Live chats L, models M, and report refresh frequency; payload generation is O(M) per chat and owner-session report patches include peer reports.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A per-chat Throttler coalesces queued triggers for that chat, while in-flight work is not cancelled. Different chats run independently and can burst concurrently.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each live chat stores a full report snapshot containing model defaults/choices. Equality prevents dispatching an unchanged individual report, but generating it still performs all three RPCs. Reports are removed on chat disposal; no unbounded post-disposal retention was found.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: ownership, disposal, report shape, equality check, and dispatch behavior are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical report/catalog size and peer-chat count vary. Disposal cleanup and equality checks bound retention and suppress unchanged dispatches, so no separate memory finding was submitted.
Scenarios.Verdict: The cross-chat burst is covered by the publication fan-out finding. Serialization growth is real but not separately reported because expected peer-chat cardinality is uncertain and cleanup is present.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering the model picker, restoring automation configuration, and switching chats
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Schema projection and picker updates are synchronous in-memory work on report/model changes; no new filesystem, database, network, subprocess, or direct IPC boundary is reached from rendering or ordinary picker reads.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of models and configuration properties when a report/catalog changes, not frame or input frequency.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Workbench observable updates run synchronously per change; model configuration writes use the existing asynchronous access surface and are scoped to the current chat when available.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The workbench keeps per-conversation overrides/preferences in maps, clears them on store reset/disposal, and does not persist host-owned report defaults as personal preferences. Observable equality suppresses unchanged session-report application.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the inspected workbench call graph; all changed projection helpers are in-memory.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog sizes are ordinarily limited; no evidence showed the added map/schema cloning on a per-frame, scroll, or keystroke path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional reportable performance regression: work is bounded in-memory projection, read-only state is cleaned up, and no hot UI boundary was introduced.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass across all 57 changed files. Submitted three findings: per-turn managed-policy resolution on the prompt critical path, serialized policy resolution after model discovery, and unbounded per-live-chat control-plane fan-out on model publication. No concrete cleanup leak, persistent cache growth, or synchronous per-frame UI regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
